title: Continuity of Hom out of $C$ is closed under extensions and shifts
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Lambda$ a condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and let $\mathcal T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be the ordinary unbounded derived category of sheaves of left $\Lambda_X$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with its shifts and distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of complexes of these modules. Let $K^\bullet=\varinjlim_i K_i^\bullet$ be its termwise colimit, with structure maps $\kappa_i:K_i^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $K_i,K$ for their images in $\mathcal T$. No common lower bound is required for this formal assertion.

For $C\in\mathcal T$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$ let
$$
\theta_{C,q}:\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C,K_i[q])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C,K[q]),\qquad [h_i]\longmapsto\kappa_i[q]\circ h_i,
$$
where the colimit is in abelian groups. Let $\mathcal C$ consist of those $C$ for which $\theta_{C,q}$ is bijective for every $q$. Then $\mathcal C$ is closed under shifts, isomorphisms and extensions: if $C'\to C\to C''\to C'[1]$ is distinguished and $C',C''\in\mathcal C$, then $C\in\mathcal C$. More generally, any finite construction by extensions, shifts and isomorphisms from any collection $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal C$ stays in $\mathcal C$. This applies in particular to any supplied family of objects $a_!L$ satisfying the comparison condition.

For the constructible specialization, assume in addition that $X$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Take $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ with the condensed coefficient conventions [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Here $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ means bounded complexes with constructible cohomology in the finite constant local model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Here a locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is a composite $a=i\circ u$ with $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For such a factorization put $a_!L=i_*u_!L$ using module pushforward [def-sfb-module-lower-star] and open extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. A lisse $\Lambda_S$-module means a module locally isomorphic for the pro-étale topology to a finite direct sum of $\Lambda_S$. If every such $a_!L$ lies in $\mathcal C$, then every object of $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal C$.

proof.text: Identify the bijectivity predicate in homContinuityLocus with the isomorphism predicate homColimitProperty by the concrete-category bijective/isomorphism equivalence.
Use the shift and isomorphism closure lemmas for homColimitProperty, transporting back through the preceding equivalence.
Use homColimitProperty_extensions for a distinguished triangle, then transport back to obtain the middle-object closure.
Instantiate ObjectProperty shift and triangulated-closed structures and apply extensionProductIter_le_of_isTriangulatedClosed₂ to obtain the finite-construction assertion.

Now impose the hypotheses of the constructible specialization. They are exactly the Noetherian-scheme and field-coefficient hypotheses of [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation]. That node says that every $M\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ has a finite witness whose entries are $a_!L[n]$ or cones of morphisms between earlier entries, up to shifts and isomorphisms. Each generator there is $a_!L[n]$ with $a_!L=i_*u_!L$ formed through the factorization $a=i\circ u$ of the locally closed immersion through the closure of its image, $u$ open and $i$ closed, and with $L$ locally free of finite rank for the pro-étale topology. That factorization is one of the open-then-closed factorizations admitted in our hypothesis and $L$ is lisse in our sense (locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of $\Lambda_S$), so the assumed membership gives $a_!L\in\mathcal C$, and step 1 puts every $a_!L[n]$ in $\mathcal C$. Induct along the witness: an entry in the generating class lies in $\mathcal C$ as just shown; an entry isomorphic to $\operatorname{Cone}(f)[m]$ for a morphism $f$ between earlier entries lies in $\mathcal C$ by the cone closure of step 5, followed by the shift and isomorphism closure of step 1. Hence the last object $M$ lies in $\mathcal C$. This includes the zero and empty-scheme cases. Only the finite constant local model constructibility occurring in the cited generation theorem is used; there is no identification with an arbitrary ring-object local finite presentation predicate.
